title: Python if, elif and else Statements
learningObjectives: Explain how python if, elif and else statements control program flow.
Predict which branch executes for given inputs.
Apply conditions to practical decision tasks.
Choose readable alternatives when control flow becomes complex.

understand.concept: An if/elif/else chain selects at most one matching branch. Python checks conditions from top to bottom; the first truthy branch runs and the remaining branches are skipped. An else branch is optional and runs only when no preceding condition matched.
understand.whyItMatters: Branch chains model choices such as grade bands, menu options and status handling.
understand.analogy: It is like a series of checkpoints: the first matching checkpoint decides which path is taken.
understand.analogyLimit: Branch order matters. A broad condition placed first can prevent a more specific condition from being reached.

explain.narrative:
## 1. if and elif

Start with `if`, then add zero or more `elif` branches. Python tests them in order.

## 2. else

An optional `else` handles every case not matched earlier. It has no condition.

## 3. First match wins

Only the first matching branch executes. Put specific conditions before broader ones when necessary.

examples.title: Choose a pass result
examples.explanation: The first condition is true, so else is skipped.

examples.title: Select a grade band
examples.explanation: The first condition is false and the second is true.

examples.title: Handle three ranges
examples.explanation: Neither comparison matches, so else executes.

examples.title: Only one branch runs
examples.explanation: The first true branch runs; the later elif is not checked.

examples.title: Order specific conditions first
examples.explanation: The conditions divide ages into ordered, non-overlapping outcomes.

practise.guidedTask: Build a three-branch program that classifies a number as positive, negative or zero.
practise.independentTask: Create a grade classifier with at least four ranges. Test boundary values and ensure each value enters exactly one branch.
hints: Use if for the first condition.
Use else for the remaining cases.
Only the first true branch executes.
practise.challenge: Find a condition-ordering bug where a broad range makes a later branch unreachable, then repair it.

questions.prompt: How many branches in an if/elif/else chain execute?
questions.explanation: Python executes only the first matching branch.

questions.prompt: Which keyword handles the remaining unmatched cases?
questions.explanation: The optional else branch runs if no prior condition is true.

questions.prompt: In what order are elif conditions checked?
questions.explanation: Python evaluates branch conditions in source order.

questions.prompt: What is important about branch order?
options: An earlier true branch prevents later branches from running
questions.answer: An earlier true branch prevents later branches from running
questions.explanation: Only the first matching branch is executed.

questions.prompt: What happens if no condition is true and there is no else?
questions.explanation: Without a matching condition or else, the chain simply continues.
